cvEn:
Son of Rachel and Nisim, Nisim Peretz was born in 1951 in Morocco. He was the only son of his parents. Nisim was born on the day his father died, and for that reason he was named after him. He began his studies at the elementary school in his hometown, and in 1963, at the age of twelve, he immigrated to Israel with his mother, and the two of them made their home in Dimona. He continued his elementary education at the Yosefthal school and completed it in the metalwork track at the Lehman Amal comprehensive high school. In addition to Hebrew, Nisim spoke French, Arabic and English. Before his conscription, he worked as a metalworker at a factory in Dimona.

At the beginning of February 1969, Nisim was drafted for compulsory service in the IDF, and after basic training he was posted to serve in the Air Force, first as a metalworker and later as a ground equipment mechanic. In February 1972, Nisim joined the regular army and served as head of the generator department in the Air Force and as an aviation technician. His commanders valued his abilities and attested that he was a disciplined, loyal and decent soldier, a very skilled professional, thrifty, resourceful, caring and mature in his approach. Nisim had professional seniority and rich experience, and he advanced matters within his area of responsibility. Throughout, he showed a desire to advance. Nisim served in the regular army for some eighteen years, and during his service he received decorations for his participation in the Yom Kippur War and the Peace for Galilee operation, as well as the operational service ribbon.

In 1975 he married Tamar, and the two made their home in Dimona, where they raised their three children. In early 1990, Nisim fell ill and was hospitalized at Soroka Hospital. Nisim fought his illness, but on 21 Adar 5750 (18 March 1990) the illness overcame him. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Dimona. He left behind his wife Tamar, a son Ronen, and two daughters, Odelia and Hali. He was thirty-nine years old at his death. After his death, Nisim was posthumously promoted to the rank of Master Sergeant. In his letter of condolence to the family, the unit commander wrote, among other things: "...Nisim served as an example and a model in the level of performance of his duties that he demonstrated. He was both a friend and a commander. He trained many soldiers who achieved high results thanks to his professionalism, integrity and modesty..."
